newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine may stop govt buying of domestic grain.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine may stop govt buying of domestic grain.

text.p: Ukraine may cease its Soviet-era practice of government purchases of set amounts of domestic grain, the deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture said on Thursday.
"It is planned for the government to stop the state orders, which we have been doing for years," Mykhailo Zubets, also agriculture minister, told a news conference.

He did not say when the system would end, but top government officials have said the scheme, under which the government buys grain at set prices, often below market levels and often on non-cash terms, would stop next year.

"We plan to adopt market practices so that the government buys grain just like commercial businesses and is an active player on the market," Zubets said as he outlined plans to reform a farm sector still dependent on government hand-outs.
The government said earlier it planned to buy 5.88 million tonnes from the 1997 crop compared with 5.0 million tonnes purchased from last year's crop.
